name: Late-onset Localized Junctional Epidermolysis Bullosa-Intellectual Disability Syndrome
aliases: Localized Junctional Epidermolysis Bullosa with Intellectual Disability
Late-onset Junctional EB with Cognitive Impairment

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Late-onset Localized Junctional Epidermolysis Bullosa-Intellectual Disability Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of localized blistering and skin fragility with onset in adolescence or adulthood
Documented intellectual disability ranging from mild to moderate severity
Skin biopsy showing junctional epidermolysis bullosa with cleavage within the lamina lucida
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes encoding laminin-332 or related junctional EB proteins
Exclusion of other forms of epidermolysis bullosa and causes of intellectual disability

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (clinical presentation, intellectual disability, and histopathology) must be met for diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is supportive but not mandatory; diagnosis relies heavily on clinical and histopathological correlation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized skin blistering with minimal trauma
searchTerms: skin blisters forming with little injury

pathognomonic.symptomName: Junctional cleavage plane on skin biopsy
searchTerms: skin biopsy showing separation at junction layer
split between skin layers on biopsy

common.symptomName: Skin fragility localized to acral areas
searchTerms: fragile skin on hands and feet
delayed learning of motor and cognitive skills

laboratory: Possible mild elevation of inflammatory markers during blistering episodes
imaging: Brain MRI may show nonspecific mild cortical atrophy in some cases
genetic: Pathogenic variants in LAMA3, LAMB3, or LAMC2 genes encoding laminin-332 subunits
other: Skin biopsy with immunofluorescence mapping confirming junctional cleavage

distinguishingFeatures: Onset in infancy or early childhood

redFlags: Onset of blistering after childhood with localized distribution
Presence of intellectual disability alongside skin findings
references: Orphanet: Late-onset localized junctional epidermolysis bullosa-intellectual disability syndrome. ORPHA:231556
Fine JD, et al. Inherited epidermolysis bullosa: updated recommendations on diagnosis and classification. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2020.
Smith FJD, et al. Junctional epidermolysis bullosa with intellectual disability: clinical and molecular characterization. Am J Med Genet A. 2018.
